Complete the square in t and apply the Tan⁻¹ formula

insider_note: Compare this with the same integral without the +6: the extra constant in the denominator is what turns the completed square from a DIFFERENCE (log formula) into a SUM (Tan⁻¹ formula) — the same substitution, a genuinely different standard result at the end.

steps.label: Set up the tan(x/2) substitution
steps.why: The same universal substitution t = tan(x/2), now applied to a denominator that also carries a constant term.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the constant 6 needs the common denominator (1+t²) too, exactly as the sinx and cosx terms do.
Sign error copying the cosx formula.
steps.memory_tip: Every term in the denominator — trig ratios AND any constant — goes over the same (1+t²).

steps.label: Substitute and simplify to a rational function of t
steps.why: The (1+t²) factors cancel as before, but this time the numerator's −t² and +6t² combine to leave a genuine quadratic 3t²+8t+9, not a linear expression.
common_mistakes: Combining −3t² (from cosx) and 6t² (from the constant) with the wrong sign, giving a different quadratic.
Not multiplying the constant 6 by BOTH parts of (1+t²).
steps.memory_tip: 6·(1+t²) contributes +6 AND +6t² — both pieces must land in the working, not just the constant part.

steps.label: Complete the square in t and apply the Tan⁻¹ formula
steps.why: This time the completed square leaves a POSITIVE constant, 11/9, so the quadratic is a sum of squares — the Tan⁻¹ formula applies here, unlike the log formula a DIFFERENCE of squares needs.
common_mistakes: Reaching for the log formula out of habit, copying the difference-of-squares method without checking the sign.
steps.memory_tip: Positive constant after completing the square ⇒ Tan⁻¹; negative ⇒ log — check the sign every time.

steps.label: Back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: Clearing the internal thirds inside the Tan⁻¹ argument and substituting tan(x/2) back for t returns the answer to the variable the question was asked in.
common_mistakes: Leaving the argument as the un-simplified (t+4/3)/(√11/3) instead of clearing to (3t+4)/√11.
Forgetting to substitute tan(x/2) back in for t.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply top and bottom of the inner fraction by 3 to clear the thirds, then swap t for tan(x/2).
